Report scope: a round checks changes and affected dependants; final acceptance reconciles the full approved inventory.

Declare supported viewports and theme/locale combinations from target use. Inspect every route's primary state at every declared viewport and variant. Exercise each additional critical state in every declared variant, extending viewport coverage where layout or risk differs. Preserve user-requested exhaustive coverage and record approved exclusions with their reasons. Include short heights and actual narrow-input conditions where supported; fixed dimensions are project choices.

Treat the formal SPEC as a design increment in the current product. Identify its experience goal, consequential visual responsibilities and actual review entry, then distinguish two verification responsibilities:

- **Current SPEC quality:** inspect the concrete relationships this increment promises, through the relevant detail, whole context and complete behavior. A page-level overview can leave an input's typography, material or changing geometry unexamined. A local screenshot can leave continuous motion and shared state unexamined.
- **Related-product integrity:** inspect existing regions, shared systems, states and journeys affected by the change. A strong isolated component cannot establish that reading width, focus, scrolling, foreground legibility or the product's visual language still work together.

Keep research/observation scope, primary design/implementation scope and integration/regression scope separately understandable in existing records. Broad research does not automatically broaden the promised implementation. A small implementation can require wider regression. Choose checks from actual dependencies and changed conditions, preserving explicit user coverage requirements; this does not require repeating every previous product study.

For a composer-height change, observe text growth, send, response growth and user-controlled scrolling with the neighboring reading space. If these jointly carry the goal, keep the relationship in the current SPEC's review scope. For a shared font change, inspect dependent pages' wrapping, hierarchy, control geometry and relevant locales rather than judging only the specimen. For motion, observe trigger, preparation, progression, settling, reversal and interruption where applicable, including other components that must remain spatially or semantically continuous. For a dynamic background, examine moving emphasis and foreground reading/input conditions in the assembled task. A static frame, component-area estimate or passing geometry assertion supports only its actual observation.

Trace each important quality through its observed reference, actual mature implementation, faithful authorized design translation or qualifying authorized W1–W3 work, current rendered result and remaining difference. Judge scope suitability, research depth and visual maturity from that evidence. Formal SPEC identity, record structure, actual implementation and perceived quality require separate conclusions; neither a smaller scope nor a completed structural report establishes them.

When an important visual object or connected interaction first supports meaningful review, inspect it in the current project and present the actual result in the conversation. Keep this opportunity early enough to correct consequential relationships before they become a wider implementation foundation. A partial implementation can support a useful review when its working scope and remaining conditions are explicit. For a research-only or direction task, show the relevant inspectable design material and identify what it establishes.

Use the [four evidence roles](component-sourcing.md#confirm-consequential-parts-in-a-local-trial) to make the subject clear. Put the current result beside the relevant target relationship or comparison, explain what is already visible and retain significant differences. Show a real preview, image or suitable episode through the host's supported surface; a written claim or a file saved out of view does not replace the consequential result. Reuse evidence gathered for the design decision rather than creating a separate presentation package.

Choose evidence by the promised quality: useful-scale images can show type, composition and material; growth, scrolling, dragging and asynchronous transitions need the relevant continuous operation or playback. Apply the temporal method below, preserving natural-speed judgment and any unavailable viewing capability. A few attractive frames cannot establish the intervals between them. A simple repair may combine target, corrected result and scoped check in one delivery; complex work benefits from seeing defining relationships while they remain adjustable. Presenting an early result establishes an opportunity to inspect, not completed verification or user approval.

## Match assurance to impact

Check local changes in context, shared changes across dependants and journeys through transitions/recovery. Integration needs visual and business evidence; depth follows consequence, variability and decision value.

Explain sampling and remaining conditions. Package checks, scenarios, viewed pixels, executed interactions, user research and real integration establish different facts; comparative model evaluations are separate research.
Choose the next observation by the unresolved experience question. Assess these dimensions together, at the scope of the proposed decision:
| Inspection depth | The consequential composition, type, material, proportions and details have actually been examined |
| Evidence relevance | Conditions and subject answer this product's question, including its user's intended version or platform |

Quantity cannot compensate for a missing dimension. Multiple reposts share an origin; a detailed still leaves movement unresolved. Separate actual observation, source statements, professional inference and missing evidence. Corroborate consequential claims through appropriate text, renders or operation; preserve conflicts for investigation rather than silently merging versions or users.

Before broader implementation, revisit target understanding, explored alternatives, the observed reason for selection, implementation fit and uncertainty that could overturn it. A bounded trial can resolve fit without claiming the target is already met. After integration, check experience alignment, visual craft, distinctive expression and engineering reliability on the real task; carry residual gaps at their own scope. The [analysis](analysis.md) and [sourcing](component-sourcing.md) methods guide whether further discovery or trial is valuable.

Record video dimensions/scaling separately. [Playwright video](https://playwright.dev/docs/videos) can scale output and needs context closure to finish writing. Retain full-size stills for small type or optical detail.

Record display scaling. Fitted pages/contact sheets support overview; reading and optical judgments need intended use scale. Retain crop location and neighbors; return from enlargement to normal scale to judge its effect.

Open required images and relevant video/ordered frames. Files, DOM snapshots and capture commands establish availability; visual inspection requires viewing pixels. Select perceptual dimensions from the actual subject and task.

Run tasks through real affordances: navigation, keyboard focus, input retention, loading, errors and recovery. Compare related pages' anchors and visual language under corresponding conditions; page responsibilities can justify different compositions.

Use geometry, contrast, accessibility, console/network evidence and image differences to locate causes or verify measured properties. Pixels support perceived balance, material and motion judgments; user comprehension requires user observation.

Attribute observations to **carrier page, player, depicted product UI or its displayed work/content**. Carrier DOM/requests explain its page/player; the depicted application needs corresponding evidence. Identify edited promotion, authored demo or actual operation, retaining source/version and conditions. Edited media supports displayed relationships; response, failure and completion require runtime evidence.

Observe **pre-trigger state → action → first feedback → progression → settled result** in references, candidates, trials and runtime. Demos expose a selected flow; authorized operations can fill return, interruption or recovery gaps. Playback, live observation or media analysis supplies inspection; acquisition alone does not.

Choose the window from the behavior:

When supported, view normally, pause/replay or enlarge relevant frames, then return to normal speed to judge rhythm. Apply the [seven temporal qualities](interaction-and-variants.md#read-motion-through-perceptible-qualities), including hidden/replacement intervals and surrounding elements.

Retain frame order, actual timestamps/event offsets, cadence, actions/states and clock source; use capture-time brackets when presentation instants are unknown. Planned screenshot delays do not establish actual intervals.

Tie episodes/frames to runs or recordings; mark resets, reruns and edits. Contact sheets locate events; open important frames at useful size and connecting intervals for continuity. Retain state, order and gaps across journeys.

Let behavior determine duration, change speed sampling density, and design impact analysis depth. Extend for seams, flashes, overlap, jumps or late updates; mark omissions. Sparse samples establish sampled states, not intervening continuity. Without playback, inspect ordered frames and leave playback-dependent claims pending. Acquisition, actual inspection and sufficient support remain distinct; metadata or a poster establishes neither playback nor continuity.

For reproducible authored timelines or regression probes, fix source, stage/viewport, content, fonts, assets, initial state and relevant seeds; seek explicit times when supported. Record controlled clocks/mechanisms and remaining nondeterminism. Compare progression, reset and loop seams through contact sheets and full playback. Frame stepping, slowed playback and a [simulated clock](https://playwright.dev/docs/clock) reveal ordering/geometry; natural-time observation separately establishes experienced pacing. Capture overhead and environment still apply; frame-delivery claims need runtime traces.

Check capture settings. [Disabling screenshot animations](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-screenshot-option-animations) can fast-forward finite animations and reset infinite ones: use that output for declared static comparison, with motion enabled in a separate natural-progression run. Record masks, injected styles and overlays that alter evidence; preserve the indicator when examining focus/caret.

Locate the change within its interval, such as a reversing card shifting against its stationary action. Test causes with state, layout, animation ownership or traces; missing frames may reflect capture. After repair, reinspect the interval and complete episode/return.

## Findings and repair

Connect the viewed state/interval, phenomenon, task/perceptual effect, intent, cause to test, repair and recheck. Prioritize blocked tasks, hidden controls, shared defects and consequential composition/continuity problems.

Locate the gap: unsuitable source, damaged adaptation, content/structure mismatch, conflicting resources or an unworkable target. Correct the responsible asset, token, component, timing, state or data contract and recheck affected journeys. Preserve the accepted art direction while resolving concrete reading, operation or runtime problems; change its scope explicitly when necessary. Keep observation and causal inference distinct.

When a finding materially changes the design judgment, show the observed discrepancy and its affected relationships through the [design-event disclosure principle](workflow.md#make-consequential-design-work-observable). Explain the cause being tested, the corrective direction and what must be reinspected; keep uncertain causes distinguishable from visible facts. Then carry out the relevant research, replacement or repair and inspect the changed result at the original problem's scope and its affected neighbors. A clipping wrapper may need adaptation repair, while lost material contrast may require a different composition or source. Keep the finding active in the current model until the evidence or an explicit scope decision changes its responsibility. A problem report, installed resource or passing functional test cannot settle an unresolved visual promise.

New evidence can improve the SPEC. If the target remains unattainable, state the gap, effect and viable options for the consequential user decision. Integration progress does not establish quality acceptance; preserve the agreed standard until its scope or direction is explicitly revised.

Keep research, correction and reinspection directed at an existing SPEC's promised experience within that SPEC. A new formal increment requires a distinct design purpose and review boundary. When evidence warrants splitting or redrawing an active SPEC, record the reason, retained target, transferred responsibility and unresolved findings in the current model. Carry the original finding and its actual condition into the receiving scope; creating a later SPEC does not resolve it. Inspect the remaining increment against its stated responsibility and report the complete product's still-open goals accurately.

## Comparing SPEC and connected product

Distinguish **Source Fidelity** from **Perceptual Quality**. Fidelity protects an identified approved design or adopted source: structure, assets, type, proportion, material and behavior. Perceptual review judges the actual composition, craft and continuous experience. Authorized original work has its own quality and fidelity boundary; reference study alone supplies neither authorization nor mature implementation adoption.

For strict restoration, identify the exact target/revision and intended differences; match content, viewport, pixel ratio/zoom, browser/rendering conditions, fonts, themes, locales and event phase. Use overlays, regional differences or pixel metrics to locate deviations, with task-justified tolerances and disclosed masks. Diagnose rendering variation; a similarity score cannot certify design quality.

Align episodes by meaningful events/object identity; explain latency/data differences. Keep reproducible fixtures beside real-service evidence. Revise an approved target explicitly when new evidence warrants it.

## Status meanings

- `planned`: declared coverage, not yet executed.
- `pass`: the specified check was executed, inspected where visual, and has evidence.
- `fail`: an observed issue remains.
- `blocked`: a required capability, resource or permission is unavailable.
- `waived`: an explicitly accepted exception with reason, scope and approver.

Distinguish capture, visual inspection and interaction verification. Without a usable image/video viewer, capture/runtime checks can proceed while visual judgment remains pending. State the missing capability and continue independent work. After changes, recapture affected views/episodes before extending claims; reconcile revisions before carrying approval forward.

## Decide when to present the round

For formal delivery, present inspectable work with required checks complete, blockers resolved and uncertainty scoped. Design review can precede integration. Show consequential candidates, episodes or before/after views; keep agent judgment and user approval separate.

Present the formal increment's actual working or renderable result in its product context. Explain what it inherited or changed, the important resource choice, observed local quality, related-product checks, remaining gaps and the next useful increment. Keep Overview, Design Detail and Execution & Assurance consistent with the same current design information. Writing the record is not the user-facing delivery: the conversation should provide the evidence and choices needed to judge this result without reading every internal note. Earlier work can be presented provisionally when that helps a decision, with its unfinished scope explicit.

## Lightweight checker

`python <skill-dir>/scripts/check_manifest.py --project-root . --view checks --json`

This optional inspector describes declared target/check references and local file facts. The connections view presents connection and approval declarations without judging their sufficiency. Legacy review/finish arguments are display aliases only. It cannot launch browsers, view pixels, verify identity, decide actions or certify completion. Reuse adequate project matrices and assess actual coverage independently.

| How does a supported animation progress? | [Animations](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/css/animations) supports pause, replay and timeline inspection; verify the rendering mechanism's coverage |

| Did the runtime deliver frames and respond as intended? | [Performance traces](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/performance/reference) support measured timing; captured filmstrips retain their sampling limits |

Use scripts within authorized page/resource access. Data changes, messages and transactions retain their authorization; private media/traces stay in authorized destinations. Capabilities supply evidence, not automatic access or conclusions. [Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html) and [interaction patterns](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) guide accessibility checks.

Use the [multiscale method](principles.md) at normal use scale: whole impression, composition, consequential regions/details, then whole task. Retain neighbors and context. After correction, recheck hierarchy across affected states, pages and episodes; an enlarged difference matters when it changes the intended-size result.

“The summary is separated by most of the viewport” is observed; “the gap weakens grouping” is an interpretation. Test causes through comparison or implementation evidence. Unseen interaction and audience response remain unverified.

Assess task correctness and accessible operation, communication clarity, identity/coherence and implementation craft as complementary obligations rather than a weighted score that can hide a critical failure. Automated geometry, console, network and accessibility checks establish their measured properties; source images, actual human-visible rendering and meaningful task operation are still needed to judge the visual result.
## Diagnose and improve the strongest relationship
Identify the weak relationship before tuning parameters. Repair structure or meaning, then detail. Compare equivalent conditions; group related changes when their effects remain attributable.

Assess **experience validity** and **expressive completion** independently: can people understand and complete the task reliably, and does the promised art direction appear with mature assets, composition, detail and motion? Strength in one cannot compensate for a gap in the other. Inspect first encounter, populated core work, long content, repeated use and related views. A different appearance can meet the quality target; names or averaged scores cannot establish it.
## Verify the publishing medium

For documentation, inspect hierarchy, selectable text, copyable commands, links, alt text, image width, narrow code/table handling and declared variants in supported markup. Check hidden content through the actual scroll/disclosure mechanism. A local approximation identifies its renderer; the publishing host needs its own readback and visible inspection.

A working product needs semantic controls, actual content/state and boundary checks. A product demonstration needs an accurate representative flow and disclosed staging. Authored visual work can use fixed layers/stage/timing; inspect fidelity, holds, transitions, resets/seams and final encoded playback. A video of a UI does not establish its operability. Verify diagram semantics and generated assets' delivered bytes alongside editable sources; match claims to the observed medium.

Keep design research and the product interface at their respective audiences. Check that the product's content, controls, hierarchy and dynamic feedback serve the user's actual task. Internal SPEC identifiers, evidence tables and explanations of implementation principles belong in design records unless the product's own task calls for them. Demonstrate promised depth, material or motion in the actual interface; a label describing a quality cannot establish its presence. Assess the initial increment for a sufficiently resolved representative experience and honest unavailable features, so later SPECs inherit a useful foundation.
## Retain lessons with boundaries

Retain a lesson's problem, mechanism, conditions, editable realization, evidence and limits. Keep project preferences local; propose portable examples through authorized maintenance. Explanatory examples support future decisions, while model improvement needs its own evidence.
## Validate resource adoption in context

Inspect the [four objects](component-sourcing.md#confirm-consequential-parts-in-a-local-trial) separately: reference, original demo, current-project trial and assembled journey. Trial consequential parts before expansion under the content, fonts, language, theme and states that could change fit; recheck combined attention, cost, cleanup and service boundaries.

Keep research, comparison, trial, adoption and inspection distinct. Retain source/revision, settings, viewed states/episodes, changes and gaps. Supplied files need inspection; record/retrieval checks establish only their mechanics.
## Verify the design decision chain

Connect user intent, experience hypothesis, research question, product/user evidence, viewed relationships, candidate comparison, adopted implementation and result. Check primary action, continuation and selection authority; provisional choices retain their status.

Re-answer research questions beside the preview with current content, comparable scale/density and corresponding interaction phases. Trace the desired quality to the adopted implementation, adaptation and observed result. Exercise first use, active work and resume. Fixture results, product acceptance, agent evaluation and user research retain separate scope.
## Inspect inherited design value

Identify retained, changed and authorized original mechanisms in code/assets and runtime. Attribution or a package name proves neither adopted scope nor quality. Check the [construction boundary](component-sourcing.md#default-deny-original-ui-construction) before treating new visual responsibility as ordinary adaptation. Compare local craft, whole-page hierarchy, proportions, reading rhythm and continuity. Revalidate authorized rewritten layout/state/motion independently; upstream maturity covers retained mechanisms. Judge reuse by consequential responsibilities fulfilled, not dependency totals or code share.
### Verify retained craft and the whole product separately

Keep **Resource Acquisition**, **Resource Adoption** and **Craft Retention** at their actual proof boundaries. Check the selected source and revision, the call site or actual placement, relevant configuration and modifications, then inspect the original demo, local trial and integrated task. A source can serve more than one role, but a demo screenshot cannot prove the project's result. Identify the meaningful source relationships before comparison; use corresponding content, font, scale, theme, viewport and temporal phase where possible, and state unavoidable differences.

Inspect whether the important composition, type, material, light, motion and state relationships still operate. A copied card that lost its light/material, a block overwritten with arbitrary spacing or a rewritten transition is not verified reuse merely because the file or import survives. Source diffs can locate changed mechanisms; actual viewing and operation determine their effect. Check related regions after local repairs, including state ownership, focus, scroll, content growth and quiet/reduced-motion states where relevant.

Keep the possibility of a negative result: using more mature resources may still reduce whole-product quality. Inspect competing focal points, incompatible typography/material, fractured spacing, motion interference, duplicate listeners/engines, dependency/payload cost and maintenance ownership. Retain the counterexample and improve composition, source selection or adaptation; do not respond with a higher resource-count requirement. Compare actual delivered quality, behavior and engineering cost independently.

For W1–W3 work, examine the actual qualification, scoped user authorization, unchanged mature foundation and independently checked new relationship. A successful render cannot retroactively authorize original construction. A structural record of an exception does not certify its necessity. For a technical probe, confirm that its research result remains distinguishable from formal visual delivery and that the final responsibility has an appropriate mature basis or authorized exception. Missing sources, unviewed states and unresolved quality remain open in the existing SPEC record.

## Verify assets from master to placement

Follow source/permission, transformation, derivative and actual placement. Inspect delivered bytes using the [asset-family checks](visual-assets.md#accept-the-asset-in-use): small-size silhouette/weight, type coverage, image crop/alpha/color, spatial material/export fidelity and temporal states.

Record CSS size, density, theme, viewport, content and load conditions. Exercise relevant blocked-resource, quiet, offscreen and renderer-limited states. Separate isolated craft, assembled visual quality and engineering cost. A large source preview or file signature cannot establish small-size readability, editable geometry or runtime behavior.

A browser fixture can validate integration paths when specialist production is unavailable. Report researched, executed and pending routes separately.

## Verify meaning and actual words in context

Inspect headings, navigation, labels, help, validation, status, empty, error and confirmation copy through the task. Check information at decision points and the outcome each phrase promises against its authoritative source. Include delayed, denied, partial, unknown and failed results. Review supported locales with realistic text, viewports and themes.

Check names, labels, associations, announcements, clipping, line breaks and focus. Visual review establishes reading rhythm and balance; actual user comprehension needs its own observation. Compare terminology and cross-step information responsibility, diagnose the responsible content/structure/localization/authority layer, then recheck the journey.

Choose measures from the operation people need to finish. Record task, initial data/cache, device/browser, network, workload and revision. Separate immediate feedback, usable content and authoritative completion, then trace the relevant dependency. A responsive acknowledgment can coexist with a slow service result.
| Is input acknowledged promptly? | Input delay, handler work and the next relevant presented frame | Responsiveness covers a different boundary from service completion |
| Are stressed results correct? | Object state, response ownership, partial outcomes and recovery | Optimizations preserve the required business result |

Use field observations where available and controlled runs for diagnosis/regression. [User-centric metrics](https://web.dev/articles/user-centric-performance-metrics) frame experience measures; [INP](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-inp) concerns responsiveness. Task-specific [performance measures](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Performance/measure) need explicit endpoints. Automation elapsed time and double-animation-frame samples retain those labels; they are not field INP. Video encoding rate is also distinct from application frame delivery.

Compare equivalent before/after tasks; repeat samples where variability affects the decision. Include cold/warm, realistic volume, rapid operations and relevant slow/failing boundaries. Check expiration and changed inputs when preparing or caching results. Set budgets from product needs and target devices. Report both measured benefit and cost; simulated latency, capture overhead and desktop emulation keep their limits.
## Exercise motion, growth and operational change

Use the temporal method to check full relevant motion, reverse/interrupted paths and reduced motion. Inspect object identity, face visibility, focus, hit regions and peak overlap. Vary response arrival before, during and after transition; the visible result must follow current valid state.

Exercise expansion, late assets/fonts, new records, long text and permission changes in actual scrolling regions. Inspect lower content, sticky controls, overlays, keyboard reveal and return position. Compare readable material across ready/loading/failure states. A collapsed resolved choice preserves its meaning and any permitted revision path.

For operating workflows, change a shared template and an overridden item, then inspect consuming surfaces and locales. Exercise selection across filters/pages, mixed batch outcomes, interruption and scoped retry. Confirm completed work remains and counts match actual items. Compare customer/operator views for consistent facts and appropriate action. Derive repeated-task efficiency from observed work and recovery at representative scale.
## Verify the map and the scope of each claim

Use [the evidence map](evidence-map.md) to reconcile coverage, source roles, decisions, actual implementation and checked conditions. Acquired/observed/compared, trialed/adopted, verified and owner-approved describe different facts; blocked and confirmed exceptions do not become passes. Keep outcome and evidence scope for each claim, including failures and conditions still unexamined. A parent page or journey needs its own assembled observation.

Check both directions: a decision should resolve to the evidence and actual adopted location that supports it; a changed source, condition or shared dependency should lead back to affected claims. Reference-product appearance, candidate-demo quality, local fit and integrated behavior have distinct subjects. Old evidence stays historical when applicability changes; establish a current recheck or a justified carry-forward scope.

The optional [read-only structural inspector](../scripts/check_design_evidence.py) describes the [record profile](evidence-records.md): field presence, ID lookup, local files, declared condition links and revision labels. It does not decide whether a claim is stale, evidence supports its domain, a gap blocks an action or a design is complete. The Agent examines those professional questions through actual evidence and changed conditions. Declared checks and exceptions remain separate; readable records can describe wholly unperformed work.

## Review action follow-through separately from declarations

Use [the action rules](evidence-actions.md) to determine whether a consequential gap actually led to suitable research, comparison, trial or repair. Link the resulting artifact/tool trace and decision change, not just a planned next step. Keep three conclusions separate: Skill content integrity, Agent behavior effectiveness and actual UI quality. A deterministic fixture demonstrates its authored conditions; only fresh Agent runs with auditable outputs support behavior comparisons. Preserve pending experiments as pending.

## Keep structural inspection and scoped assertions independent

Inspectors describe supplied records and theoretical coverage hints. A pass/fail
from a real browser, file-digest, package, performance or functional test retains
its precise assertion and conditions. Neither implies a professionally sufficient
experience model, adequate research, successful visual composition or overall
acceptance. Compare real renders and continuous use for those claims, and keep
owner decisions at their own scope.

A global revision label is not a blanket invalidation rule. Inspect the changed
object and actual shared dependencies, then decide which old observations remain
applicable and which need new evidence. Keep failures, exceptions and unexamined
conditions visible without merging them into satisfied coverage. A readable
record or a completed inspector run cannot finish a project.


## Verify that visual craft survived actual reuse

For a consequential adopted surface, identify the specific relationship to preserve: type-to-space rhythm, optical weight, edge/light falloff, content grouping, object continuity or interaction response. Compare **target reference → original candidate demonstration → local trial → integrated task** at their own scopes. These are observations, not completion stages awarded by a helper.

Inspect original source settings before changing them; then compare current fonts, content, density, theme, viewport and event phase. Keep retained mechanisms, configured expressions, focused patches and original work distinguishable. An imported dependency is not proof that it appears in the running interface. Establish actual call sites or asset placement, then exercise the user-visible result. Conversely, an attractive screenshot of newly authored code does not prove source implementation adoption.

Record concrete losses and repair at the responsible level. A font substitution can change wrapping; an added wrapper can clip a glow; a new background can erase a surface boundary; a reset can break source proportions; a custom event handler can displace the original state owner. Inspect the corrected local object and its neighbors, shared pages and relevant episodes. Preserve the accepted expression unless a change is explicitly justified at the product/design level.

Keep adoption benefit and implementation cost observable. For a practical comparison, retain the same task/content conditions and identify which design or behavior the mature resource actually supplied. Report setup, adaptation, discovered defects, repair and maintenance obligations separately; do not invent hours saved or infer productivity from fewer source lines. A suitable native implementation can be preferable in a supported low-impact task, while a high-impact small asset may warrant deeper research.

Judge research behavior, actual adoption, perceptual result, efficiency and stylistic adaptability independently. Resource counts, famous library names, reuse percentages and structural-check success do not establish final design quality. A controlled Agent comparison requires real independent runs with comparable inputs and auditable traces; a maintainer trial or authored browser fixture supports only its declared application. View actual renders and relevant continuous episodes, preserving sampling and device limits, before claiming a visible improvement.

## Verify delegated evidence and assembled quality separately

Auxiliary agents can provide valuable research and scoped checks; the main agent retains consequential visual judgment and final product-level verification. Directly view the material needed to decide an important candidate and inspect its actual current-product result. Do not repeat every exploratory click, but do not replace pivotal observation with a summary or a subordinate's self-evaluation.

Separate source demo, local trial and assembled interface. For each meaningful observation, retain the conditions that support it: source/version, actual content, viewport, theme, state and relevant time interval. A capture is not necessarily a viewed image; ordered frames can reveal displacement without proving natural-time smoothness. DOM assertions and tool-inclusive elapsed time do not establish perceptual continuity. Mark inaccessible or unviewed behavior explicitly.

Basic browser observation remains normal work for the main agent, researcher and integrator. Use a specialist experience observer only when extended state control, cross-interface navigation or difficult episode reproduction justifies separate attention. Prefer reliable browser interaction for web content; use authorized native computer operation when the actual task requires it. Do not allow concurrent actors to compete for one desktop or mutable browser session.

Independent challenge should test consequential assumptions and credible alternatives, not manufacture disagreement. Evidence can support retaining the current choice. Differences in theme, content density, scale or source identity may explain conflicting reports; the main agent investigates the relevant conditions rather than count votes. Engineering checks, investigator conclusions, main-agent visual review and owner acceptance keep their distinct scopes.

## Select a resolved visual asset before substituting a homemade effect

For a defining photograph, spatial object, moving background or graphic system, study mature assets and implementations while the page composition is still open. A sourced shader or authored scene may already resolve lighting, material, color progression and movement; a selected photograph may supply subject, narrative and negative space. Replacing either with the agent's default gradient or geometric placeholder changes the design target, even when the replacement is technically valid.

Judge the asset's **visual completeness at its useful scope** independently from format or production complexity. A resolved two-dimensional image may serve the intended composition better than an elaborate real-time scene. A small procedural background can carry a distinctive material, but does not provide the page's typography or functional layout. Source royalty/licensing terms, editable access and runtime compatibility remain separate adoption decisions. Public viewing does not establish permission to redistribute originals, paid templates or fonts.

For photography and illustration, compare subject relevance, crop tolerance, focal direction, depth cues, color relationships and text-safe regions with the intended page. Examine actual derivatives and narrow crops; an image's quiet area can disappear at another aspect ratio. Avoid using a screenshot of another product as editable implementation or presenting illustrative people/data as customer evidence. Prefer an actual rights-bearing source with sufficient resolution and a maintainable replacement path.

For spatial and procedural material, inspect the relationship of camera, light, texture scale, depth and motion to readable DOM content. A glossy object and a matte interface can coexist deliberately, but contradictory light directions or unrelated contrast roles need reconciliation. Preserve a chosen source's distinctive optical mechanism through configuration and focused adaptation. Replacing that mechanism with new shaders or scene logic requires the default-deny and allowlist judgment before implementation; a retained source name does not preserve its craft. Test full motion range, resize, device-pixel ratio, quiet/offscreen behavior, renderer unavailability and cleanup as relevant. Canvas-rendered text or images do not automatically inherit the semantics, selection and loading behavior of native content.

If an asset degrades in context, compare the original demonstration, local placement and assembled viewport. Determine whether the cause is crop, color treatment, density, layering, unhandled content, a changed parameter or runtime delivery. Reopen source selection when adaptation would remove the quality that justified it. Preserve a project-specific expressive direction rather than treating a technical fallback as universal artistic approval.

The main path is `init → iterate → finish`; `audit` runs throughout and optional `shape` resolves consequential uncertainty wherever it appears. Resume or combine operations from current evidence. A local refinement can finish in one round; an approved product can enter integration directly.

Connect intended experience → evidence questions → research/observation → design comparison → mature resource adoption → actual-use verification. Findings can return work to any responsible step. Use the [evidence maturity judgment](analysis.md#reason-about-uncertainty) to continue research, run a bounded trial or expand implementation. Treat the conversation as a window into professional design execution. Internal work supplies actual evidence; the Current Design Model maintains the current understanding; selected outputs let the user observe consequential findings, decisions and results. The aim is to improve feedback between research and realized UI while preserving autonomous execution. Use existing evidence and records rather than producing a parallel reporting system.

A **Design-Significant Disclosure Point** occurs when a fact, judgment or result materially affects the current experience model, visual direction, source choice, implementation commitment, quality or scope. Consider three lenses together: **design impact**, **user observation value** and **quality realization value**. Ask whether seeing this now would expose an important relationship, clarify an actual choice or reveal a mismatch early enough to affect the work. These lenses support judgment, without scores, timing quotas or required message counts. Search volume, a tool result, a saved file and an operation transition alone do not establish such an event.
### Recognize six kinds of design event
| Event | When it matters | Show the decision-useful substance |

| **A — Formal scope and quality target** | A formal SPEC begins or its commitments materially change | Experience objective, owned qualities, necessary relationships, inherited foundation and reason for the boundary; preserve the complete product goal. |
| **B — Research finding** | Actual evidence changes understanding of the target or problem | The observed subject and conditions, significant visual or temporal relationship, supported judgment and effect on the current design. |
| **C — Design or mature-resource choice** | Art direction, a resource or a realization strategy will carry consequential quality | Actual candidate or useful comparison, meaningful differences, current choice and its reason, qualities to preserve and whether adoption still needs a trial. |
| **D — First reviewable result** | An important visual object or interaction first becomes meaningfully inspectable | The actual trial or product result, its relation to the target, qualities observed and material gaps; use evidence suited to the owned quality. |
| **E — Material mismatch and reconsideration** | A target mismatch, adaptation failure, insufficient quality or scope problem changes the next work | Observed symptom, affected relationships, facts versus possible causes, responsible design level, correction and necessary reinspection. |
| **F — Formal increment delivery** | The increment has an actual result to hand over | Operable/renderable result, meaningful comparison, actual adopted sources, scoped observations, remaining gaps and contribution to the evolving product. |

These kinds can recur, overlap or never arise in a task. An operation can produce several events, and several operations can contribute to one useful presentation. Preserve the information represented by A and F for a formal increment; give D particular priority for complex work so its first meaningful result becomes visible before broad dependent work inherits it. For a small correction, purpose, change and verification can fit in one concise delivery. For research-only work, the reviewable result may be an inspected comparison, annotated actual reference or design proposal, identified as such; a runnable product is not implied.

B, C and E carry a disclosure responsibility when their design impact warrants it. Do not manufacture a new finding, comparison or failure to populate the table. A routine icon replacement, search-query revision or inherited control adjustment usually stays within ordinary work. An unexpected mature block or expressive cross-domain reference can merit disclosure when its concrete relationships change the design. Resource-platform categories organize discovery, not the conversation's required headings.

### Present the consequence, then continue the work

Select the useful parts of **observation → professional judgment → decision/action → result and remaining gap**. Explain an already formed conclusion and its relevant evidence; keep internal deliberation and exhaustive search history out of the presentation. Separate what was seen from a causal hypothesis, a provisional selection from adopted code, and a planned check from its actual result. These are causal relationships, not four compulsory fields.

Use the design object as the subject. For example, an observed composer trial can show that multiline input keeps its action row aligned while reducing message space; the important next question is whether the reader's scroll anchor survives that change. State which relationship the current source carries and which remains unverified. A count of examined components would not explain that choice. Use plain language for perceptible differences, with specialized detail where it supports the current judgment.

Prefer an actual preview, readable image/comparison or relevant continuous episode when the target is visual or temporal. Identify its object: **Target Reference**, **Candidate Demo**, **Local Trial** or **Integrated UI**. A label in natural prose is enough; one event need not display all four. A local render establishes that trial's appearance, while integrated quality requires viewing the assembled product. Static captures can explain type or material; motion, scrolling and asynchronous relations need the relevant continuous observation. See [verification](verification.md) for capture and claim boundaries.

When the first result reveals a material gap, use it to change the next action: revisit the target interpretation, resource, adaptation, content, composition or runtime mechanism at the responsible level, then inspect the repaired relationship and affected neighbors. Keep an existing quality obligation in the active SPEC. Repartition only with a supported new boundary and preserved original commitments. An empty shell is not a meaningful first result, and documenting a problem does not resolve it. Small differences outside the agreed quality responsibility do not require unbounded refinement.

Keep **Disclosure**, **Review** and **Approval** distinct. Disclosure makes an event available; review requires actual examination; approval requires an actual decision with its stated scope. Existing execution authority permits continued work without implying review or acceptance of a new result. Presentation alone establishes neither user review nor assent. Continue authorized choices and repairs after showing them. Request a decision only when a consequential unresolved direction, material change to a confirmed commitment or external action actually requires one under the existing authority model; continue independent supported work.

For an important resource choice, show which mature implementation will carry the SPEC's main visual quality and why it fits. At the first integrated result, show retained craft and consequential differences; at a material source mismatch, show the damaged relationship and the next adaptation or replacement. For an original exception, state the concrete necessity, bounded original responsibility, retained mature work, actual authorization and verification scope. Present existing authorization as context, not a repeated permission request. An unresolved authorization requires a specific user decision only after useful independent work has been completed. Ordinary resource searches, installation and configuration remain autonomous.

Use **Selective Strong Disclosure**: make important commitments, consequential choices, first meaningful results, major mismatches and delivery visible when they occur, while merging related low-impact events and omitting invented ones. Reuse research evidence already produced for design judgment. Maintain the current model when a disclosed choice changes; the old message remains history rather than an irrevocable design decision. Presentation detail follows the active SPEC's qualities: background work may need material/foreground comparison, while streaming work may need scroll and interruption evidence. Neither output quantity nor polished reporting certifies research, implementation or quality. Host-required progress messages retain their own purpose and do not become extra design milestones.

Read requirements, accepted decisions, code, actual screens, dependencies and run/test instructions. Separate required behavior, explicit aesthetic goals and revisable conventions. Establish people, primary working objects, task loop, result location, content authority and operating conditions. Distinguish a live product, representative demo and authored output. View the normal-scale whole; retain important unobserved conditions, asset rights and production capabilities.

Expand a named reference into the relevant working experience, structure, visual qualities and time relationships. Separate this user's intent, audience expectations and product facts; preserve relevant version/platform/history. Without a named reference, find mature task-level and expressive references. Form revisable hypotheses before broad resource searches, then [plan evidence around the experience](analysis.md#plan-evidence-around-the-experience): important pages, states, transitions and relationships, with appropriate text, visual and behavioral sources.

Record established facts, assumptions and high-impact questions compactly. Preserve functional contracts and assess current presentation against the target. Init is sufficient when the agent can explain the task, preserve constraints and choose a justified next action. Continue an implementation request into shape or iterate; a planning request ends with its requested decision support.

Preserve the complete product goal separately from the first formal SPEC. Identify the current implementation and applicable mature foundations, then find the consequential visual objects, state/time relationships and shared dependencies that may need concentrated work. Use the [minimum sufficient experience closure](analysis.md#choose-a-bounded-increment) to form a provisional structure of meaningful candidate SPECs, their important dependencies and a justified first priority. A candidate is planning context, not an already started formal increment or a promise of a permanently fixed sequence. Keep important goals with uncertain boundaries visible as open planning questions.

Present that understanding in the conversation: the intended overall result, the current foundation, the proposed increments and why the first scope can be completed and reviewed well. State what could change the grouping. A complete mature implementation may support a larger first increment; uncertain interaction relationships may need further study before later boundaries become useful. For a new product, select a representative core experience with visual quality worth carrying forward. Continue authorized research and implementation without requiring approval for ordinary planning refinements.

Use shape for requested exploration or unresolved choices affecting product model, page responsibilities, identity or feasibility. Complete the open parts of supplied direction; an open brief receives an agent-led recommendation with inspectable evidence.

1. **Frame the question.** Connect user intent, facts, task and aesthetic goals to the uncertainty that could change the choice. Keep confirmed needs, supported conventions and hypotheses distinct.
2. **Map experience and evidence.** Establish affected objects, entries/exits, states, page relationships and return/recovery. Select text, actual views and continuous behavior evidence for the relevant version, platform and use.
3. **Explore and revise.** Research functional, expressive and implementation sources together. Follow clues through reading, playback and operation; apply the [perceptual method](principles.md). Let findings change the next question, source or experiment. Explore independent and cross-domain work where it could improve the result.
4. **Compare directions.** Form a concept through content, representation, voice, hierarchy, type, material and motion. Challenge the leading option with materially different advantages. Compare equivalent tasks/content at similar completion, including populated core use. Preserve explicit artistic requirements.
5. **Establish implementation fit.** Inspect candidates' original demos, states, source and terms, including existing work. Prefer the highest suitable reuse level and identify any source gap; a gap triggers further discovery, adaptation or a qualifying W1–W3 judgment rather than ordinary custom construction. Consider compatibility and total delivery cost; read integration guidance for real business boundaries.
6. **Trial consequential parts.** Use current fonts, content, themes, containers and meaningful states. Compare the reference, original demo and local result at corresponding scale and event phases. Adapt, replace or revisit the target according to what the trial reveals.
7. **Carry the decision forward.** Present focused options when unresolved alternatives materially change direction. Clear intent, approval or delegated autonomy supports continued work. Retain the selected/provisional direction, evidence, adaptations and open questions beside the result.

For repeated/asynchronous work, examine preparation on entry, requests on intent, immediate feedback and later confirmation. Decide preloading, parallel work or caching from cost, freshness, authority and actual latency. For maintained content, establish source ownership, defaults/overrides and operator selection/recovery before broad implementation.

Choose research, trial or expansion by what the evidence supports. Similar new results permit convergence when important questions and alternatives have been examined; an unmet defining quality remains open. An implementation request proceeds through needed trials, while proposal-only work labels them pending. Reuse matching-condition evidence and reopen decisions when findings warrant it. Keep records proportional to the choice.

**Orient and choose.** Reconcile feedback, accepted decisions, current code, incomplete journeys and findings. A continuation request is sufficient: choose and state the next useful outcome. Continue the active SPEC when fulfilling its established objective or resolving its quality gaps. Begin a new formal SPEC when undertaking a new cohesive design objective with its own meaningful review boundary; an additional search, repair or execution pass remains internal work.

**Define the slice.** Identify affected pages/states, dependencies, intended user outcome and observation conditions. Keep connected tasks and shared families coherent. State the formal SPEC's quality responsibility, the objects and relationships that must be handled together, and the applicable current-product decisions it inherits. Distinguish research/observation, primary design/implementation and integration/regression scopes. Apply the analysis method to keep, split, merge or redraw the proposed boundary; explain important scope choices and their product implications to the user before broad work depends on them.

**Research and select.** Reuse supported direction or resolve material uncertainty through shape. Pair target qualities with concrete implementation candidates and inspect their actual demos. Let discoveries refine content, assets and layout. Use the [sourcing loop](component-sourcing.md#follow-visual-clues-to-answer-design-questions) to turn unresolved questions into further search, comparison or trial. Seek alternative evidence when access fails and consolidate necessary user assistance after feasible research. Keep original construction outside normal choices; use the [closed exception allowlist](component-sourcing.md#closed-original-construction-allowlist) only for a demonstrated qualifying need with actual scoped authorization.

**Establish the implementation foundation.** For each important quality owned by this SPEC, identify the actual mature page, block, component, asset or established system that will carry it. Shared source responsibility can cover many sub-elements; do not split simple backgrounds, spacing, borders or motion out of a coherent source merely to hand-build them. Keep unresolved responsibilities open and advance independent supported work. Distinguish ordinary configuration/integration from any genuine original scope and locate its W1–W3 authorization before doing that work.

**Trial and adapt.** Work in the existing project. Trial high-impact choices with real or identified fixture content, fonts, themes, extremes and states before expansion. Preserve valuable source relationships through configuration, composition and focused changes. Connect business actions at their owner. Recheck affected mechanisms and replace candidates whose fit fails.

Use research and trial findings to reconsider the boundary while the work is active. A mature block can unify previously separate responsibilities; an animation can expose preparation, focus or neighboring-layout dependencies that need inclusion. Update the active scope and later candidates when that improves the experience closure. Preserve the prior goal, affected unresolved issues, change reason and current responsibility in the same design records. Distinguish a justified repartition from completion, and continue repairing deficiencies still covered by the active goal. Routine candidate replacement and local refinement do not require new formal SPECs.

**Carry the concrete implementation conditions.** Keep the selected item's exact variant, revision, public configuration, dependencies, source, editable assets and delivery derivatives with the implementation. Choose the appropriate static, authored-time or live delivery boundary. Test short, typical and long real or explicitly identified fixture strings, realistic content density, locale differences and meaningful pending/empty/error states. Compose copy, type scale and spacing together. Preserve business-fact authority, source permissions and the distinction between illustrative fixture values and real product claims. A representative integration should resolve the most consequential unknown before broad reuse.

**Integrate and inspect.** Compare whole → region → detail → whole, related views and continuous use under relevant conditions. Check populated core tasks, long content, repeated operation, failure and reduced motion for usability and expression. Locate gaps in experience understanding, reference, resource, adaptation or combination; return to that level and recheck. Make necessary changes to accepted direction explicit.

Verify both the current SPEC's claimed qualities and the actual effects on existing product relationships. A local pass supports that local claim; a page-wide overview may miss the component or temporal detail this increment owns. Select the necessary related checks from actual dependencies and changed conditions, without automatically repeating unrelated product research.

For performance or operating work, observe the sequence through input, usable result, authoritative completion and recovery. Compare under named conditions. Separate feedback speed, actual task time and resource consumption; inspect position under content growth and effective content after shared/individual updates.

**Inspect the assembled responsibility boundary.** In addition to the whole composition, examine cross-page anchors, actual-size assets and crops, shared focus and scrolling, listener or motion-engine conflicts, overlapping layers, cumulative runtime cost, cleanup and quiet/loading/failure states. Verify keyboard, touch and reduced-motion behavior as relevant. A pass for an isolated component does not establish coherence after multiple resources, real services and content are combined. Repair the responsible source, adapter, composition or state owner, then revisit the affected states and pages.

**Present and continue.** Supply the working entry, important choices and inspected outcome. Connect goals, evidence, actual adoption, retained mechanisms and adaptations. Distinguish studied, compared, trialled and adopted resources; use representative frames/intervals where useful. State consequential gaps, observed conditions, approval scope and next useful work. The user need not restate the method.

Make the delivery useful in the conversation, not only in saved records. Show the actual operable or renderable increment, significant visual references/comparisons, adopted resources and observed results at a depth proportional to their design impact. Explain the contribution to the complete product and the current candidate for subsequent work. During research, surface a finding or local result when it materially changes a design choice. Link detailed records for traceability while keeping the user-facing account focused on what can be seen, used or decided.

Treat an observation as an experience to investigate; a suggested implementation is a candidate unless explicitly required. For “too large,” inspect control scale, content mass, preview scaling and whitespace. For “jumps,” inspect shared anchors, scroll, component identity and timing. In **init**, identify important visual responsibilities not yet supplied by the current functional dependencies. In optional **shape**, use craft knowledge to direct real-reference and high-completeness resource discovery while the composition is still adjustable. In **iterate**, select the useful reuse scope, inspect original demos, trial genuine content and integrate retained mechanisms through configuration/composition before targeted internal changes. In **finish**, retain exact source, variant, configuration, rights, adaptation ownership and actual outcome at the product's boundary.

These are uses of the existing workflow, not five new gates. New resource discoveries can revise art direction, and integration failures can reopen selection. The main agent remains the active designer, decision-maker and integration owner. Use auxiliary agents as optional capacity inside the existing operations, not as a second workflow or a design committee. At init or shape, independent inquiries can clarify experience models and sources; during iterate, they can deepen an important choice or source trial; audit and finish can reopen a specific source or actual-use question. Do not create a formal SPEC for each delegated investigation or repair.

Delegate in natural language with the current intent, relevant conditions and useful boundaries. Stable specialist instructions supply professional methods; the parent does not have to retype them. Researchers can pursue complete multi-round inquiries, propose candidates, compare quality and report new directions. They do not choose the final design, approve originality or declare completion. Use the parent's actual host permissions and tools. By default, proposed additional investigators return to the main agent rather than recursively expanding an autonomous team.

While an inquiry runs, continue independent, supported work: inspect current content and dependencies, prepare a representative trial, verify an established region or integrate already selected work. Do not fill a source gap with a provisional hand-built visual foundation just to stay busy. A decision that genuinely depends on absent evidence remains open; the whole project need not stop.

After a result returns, absorb findings selectively into the current model. Identify what changed, examine pivotal visual evidence yourself, compare appropriate alternatives and decide whether to continue research, request targeted evidence, trial a resource or integrate it. The main agent coordinates shared interfaces and reviews the assembled UI. A discovered missing layout, material or motion decision returns to the main agent. A failed or unavailable agent/tool leaves the quality responsibility visible. Retry where useful, narrow the question, change an authorized evidence route or investigate directly.
